topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecturer, sets out the course structure, and outlines the learning objectives for understanding cancer causation.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Endogenous Mutations, Environmental Exposure, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the fundamental origins of cancer, examining the interplay between intrinsic mutational processes, inherited predispositions, environmental exposures, and global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Biological and Molecular Mechanisms of Carcinogens and Tumor Promoters
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the specific cellular and biochemical mechanisms by which infectious agents, chemical carcinogens, radiation, and inflammatory promoters induce neoplastic transformation.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the genomic, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro experimental approaches used to determine whether exposures are mutagenic and carcinogenic.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture with a summary of environmental cancer causation and the practical risk-benefit decisions surrounding exposure.
